Lamborghini Aventador

Engine & Performance

The Aventador is powered by a V12 engine delivering over 700 hp, enabling 0-60 mph in under 3 seconds.

Design & Features

Its sharp lines, scissor doors, and lightweight carbon-fibre monocoque make it a standout in both form and function.

Why Choose It?

If you’re looking for raw power, Italian craftsmanship, and a car that turns heads wherever it goes — this is the one.

Ferrari 488 GTB
☰

Ferrari 488 GTB

Engine & Performance

The Ferrari 488 GTB uses a 3.9L twin-turbo V8 making about 661 hp, hitting 0–60 in around 3 seconds. Its dual-clutch transmission and advanced aerodynamics deliver sharp handling, quick throttle response, and supercar-level speed.

Design & Features

The 488 GTB features sleek, aerodynamic bodywork, signature side air intakes, and an aggressive front end. Inside, it has a driver-focused cockpit, premium materials, and advanced systems like Ferrari’s electronic differential and magnetic suspension.

Why Choose It?

Choose the 488 GTB for its mix of raw power, precision handling, and iconic Ferrari design. It’s fast, stylish, and engineered for both daily driving and track performance — a true balance of beauty and capability.

McLaren 720S
☰

McLaren 720S

Engine & Performance

The 720S has a 4.0L twin-turbo V8 making 710 hp, hitting 0–60 in about 2.8 seconds. It’s extremely fast, lightweight, and delivers razor-sharp handling.

Design & Features

It features a carbon-fiber chassis, butterfly doors, and a sleek aerodynamic body. Inside, the cabin is modern, minimal, and built for the driver.

Why Choose It?

Choose the 720S for its top-tier speed, striking design, and precision driving feel. It’s one of the most balanced and eye-catching supercars you can get.
